Enter a token count, such as 131072 (128K), 262144 (256K), or 1048576 (1M).

Terms, privacy policy, and compliance lists
These documents describe the current version and are available offline. Services, servers, and websites selected by you may apply their own terms.
These documents disclose current behavior but do not by themselves guarantee compliance with every store or jurisdiction. Update them whenever features or data practices change.
External services, triggers, and received data

This agreement applies to the Lyra Code Android app. Lyra Code is a local-first AI agent and file tool with no built-in cloud account. You configure model, MCP, SSH, WebDAV, FTP, and similar services yourself. By installing or using the app, you acknowledge this agreement.

Product: Lyra Code. Developer and maintainer: Soffd / Lyra Code project maintainers. Contact: https://github.com/Soffd/Lyra-Code/issues .
This agreement covers the app and bundled local features. Providers of models, websites, MCP, and remote servers selected by you remain responsible for their services and may apply separate terms.

The app offers AI chat, file management, workspace tools, web search, MCP, Termux, SSH, WebDAV, FTP/FTPS/SFTP, local servers, backup, and updates. Some features require credentials, server addresses, or system permissions.
Third-party interfaces and device capabilities may change, become unavailable, or stop working.

You must be authorized to access selected files, accounts, devices, and servers, and must comply with applicable law and provider rules. Do not use the app to intrude into systems, distribute unlawful content, infringe rights, or bypass authorization.
You are responsible for credentials, private keys, and third-party fees. Prefer secure connections such as HTTPS, SFTP, and FTPS.

AI output may be inaccurate, outdated, or unsuitable and is not professional medical, legal, or financial advice. File changes, deletion, commands, uploads, and privileged tools can cause data loss or device problems.
Review commands, paths, and diffs before execution, keep backups, and take responsibility for final actions. Confirmation prompts cannot eliminate all risk.

When you configure or invoke model APIs, search sites, MCP, Termux, Shizuku, SSH, WebDAV, file transfer, updates, or external links, data is sent directly to the relevant service. Providers may log IP addresses, requests, and access records.
Their availability, charges, content, and processing are governed by their own policies.

App code and resources are supplied under the project licenses; third-party components use their own licenses. You remain responsible for content you enter, upload, or generate.
To the extent permitted by law, maintainers are not liable for indirect loss caused by provider failures, user error, missing backups, insecure connections, privileged commands, or force majeure. Liability that cannot lawfully be excluded remains unaffected.

You may stop using the app, clear its data, or uninstall it at any time. Material changes should be published with an updated effective date.
Contact maintainers through GitHub Issues. Never post API keys, passwords, private keys, precise location, or private files in a public issue.

Lyra Code is local-first and processes data on demand. The current version requires no account and includes no advertising, behavioral analytics, or third-party crash-reporting SDK. Basic local UI and file browsing do not require unrelated personal information.

We follow lawful, fair, necessary, transparent, and purpose-limited processing. This policy covers the app; services and servers chosen by you apply their own policies.
The app is primarily local. Maintainers normally do not centrally receive local chats, files, or settings. Outbound data depends on the network features and destinations you choose.

The app may process profile details; chats, prompts, memories, attachments, and tool output; API and remote-service settings; selected files, media, and camera captures; on-demand location, device, network, and app-list data; tasks, caches, audit logs, and backups.
See the Personal Information List for purpose, timing, storage, and recipients. Sensitive permissions are used only when needed and authorized by the system.

We do not sell personal information. Selected context is sent to your configured model API. Web search, MCP, SSH, WebDAV, and file-transfer requests go to destinations you specify. Browsers or target apps process external links.
The app does not control provider retention. Review the Third-party Information List and avoid sending sensitive content to untrusted services.

Chats, settings, logs, and caches are normally stored in private app storage; workspace files remain in directories you choose. Sensitive settings use the app encryption mechanism. Data remains until you delete it, clear app data, or uninstall.
You may export local or WebDAV backups. Android may also process eligible data under device backup settings. You are responsible for exported backups.

Measures include Android sandboxing, encrypted sensitive settings, confirmations, file-scope limits, and SHA-256 checks for downloads. Network security still depends on the destination; plain HTTP or FTP can expose credentials and content.
No measure guarantees absolute security. Report issues without publicly disclosing sensitive data.

You can view, change, or delete chats, memories, model and remote-service settings; clear caches; manage backups; revoke permissions in Android settings; clear all app data; or uninstall.
For access, correction, deletion, or complaints concerning information maintainers may hold, contact the project through GitHub Issues.

The app is not specifically directed to children. Minors should use it with guardian guidance and should not submit identity, location, school, contact, or similar sensitive details to models, sites, or remote servers.

Material changes to features, permissions, third parties, or processing should be reflected in this policy and its date. Contact: https://github.com/Soffd/Lyra-Code/issues . Remove sensitive data before public feedback.

This list covers information the current version may process. “On demand” items are not read merely because the app is installed. External transmission depends on your actions, tool calls, and configuration.
Data: nickname, avatar image, and local path. Purpose: profile display in the drawer. Timing: when you edit the profile. Storage/recipient: local app data; not sent externally by default.

Data: messages, system prompts, memories, titles, attachments, selected file excerpts, tool arguments/output, and model replies. Purpose: AI chat, history, summaries, and agent tools. Timing: when you enter, attach, or send content. Storage/recipient: stored locally; necessary context is sent to the model endpoint you select.

Data: model API keys and URLs; MCP keys; SSH/WebDAV/FTP/FTPS/SFTP addresses, usernames, passwords, or private keys. Purpose: connect to services you specify. Timing: configuration and connection. Storage/recipient: sensitive settings are encrypted locally and used only to authenticate to the corresponding target. Backups may include settings.

Data: names, paths, sizes, timestamps, text, images, videos, and temporary captures within selected or authorized scope. Purpose: file management, attachments, previews, workspace tools, and transfers. Timing: selection, file-manager access, capture, or approved tool action. Storage/recipient: processed locally; sent only when you attach, upload, or approve the related action.
Device, network, and runtime data (on demand)

Data: Android/device model, CPU, memory, storage, display, battery, network type, IP/interface status, Bluetooth summary, app version, task state, and errors. Purpose: diagnostics, hardware checks, networking, and tasks. Timing: Device Information page or corresponding agent tool. Storage/recipient: mainly read live; included in a model request if used as tool output.

Data: last system location; installed-app name, package, version, size, and signature digest. Purpose: location awareness and app identification tools. Timing: after authorization and explicit tool use. Storage/recipient: read on demand; no background route history; may be sent to the active model as tool output.

Data: audit logs, tool status, downloads/schedules, AI caches, temporary uploads, and selected backup content. Purpose: restore chats, audit operations, performance, and migration. Timing: while using those features. Storage/recipient: local by default; WebDAV backups go only to your selected server.
Not actively required by this version

The app does not require a phone number, legal name, identity document, contacts, SMS, call logs, payment card, face/fingerprint template, or advertising identifier for profiling. Avoid entering such data into chats, files, or external services unless truly necessary.

The current version has no advertising, behavioral analytics, or third-party crash-reporting SDK. Open-source UI, networking, player, editor, and encryption libraries run in the app and do not independently upload personal data merely because they are included.

Examples: AndroidX/Compose, OkHttp, Media3, Sora Editor, JSch, Shizuku API, and JLatexMath for UI, networking, playback, editing, SSH, authorization, and math rendering.
No independent reporting endpoint is configured for these components. See Open-source Licenses. Android System WebView may create cookies or network logs under the policy of visited sites.
AI providers and custom compatible endpoints

Possible recipients: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or another base URL you enter. Data: API key, model, messages, prompts, context, attachments/files, and tool results. Trigger: sending a message, refreshing models, or testing connectivity after configuration. Purpose: model responses. Retention and international transfer follow the target provider policy.
Search engines, websites, and download hosts

Recipients: sites and URLs you search, visit, read, or download from. Data: query, URL, requests, IP address, browser identifier, and site-set data. Trigger: web search, page reading, links, or downloads initiated by you or an authorized agent. Purpose: retrieve and display internet content.

Recipient: operator of the MCP URL you enter. Data: auth key, tool-list requests, parameters, required context, and responses. Trigger: enabling MCP and invoking its tools. Purpose: extend agent features. Avoid unknown or plain-HTTP services.
Remote hosts, storage, and local companion apps

Recipients: SSH, WebDAV, FTP/FTPS/SFTP servers you specify, plus local Termux, Termux:API, or Shizuku. Data: address, account, credentials, commands, paths, uploaded files, and results. Trigger: configured and approved connection, command, transfer, or backup. Purpose: remote management, transfer, and local command execution.

Recipient: configured manifest and APK hosts, potentially the official site or source hosting platform. Data: requests normally expose IP address, time, app version, and standard HTTP headers, but not chats or local files. Trigger: daily or manual checks and downloads. Purpose: discover and install releases.

Recipients: lyracode.app, GitHub, Gitee, QQ, Discord, and similar sites. Data: normal access data sent by the browser or target app under its policy. Trigger: you tap an About-page link. Purpose: project information, feedback, or community access.

Permissions are requested for features or declared in the Manifest. Refusing a non-essential permission leaves unrelated local features available, while the corresponding camera, location, notification, file, app-identification, or command feature may not work.

INTERNET: model APIs, web, MCP, remote servers, and updates. ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE: connectivity and diagnostics. CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE: LAN and multicast-related features.
These are normal Android permissions and generate requests only when network features are used.

ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION / ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION: read the latest system location for the “current location” tool after authorization. The app does not build a background route history. Revoke at any time in system settings.
CAMERA: capture a temporary image when you choose a photo attachment. The app does not capture in the background. Text chat and file selection remain available if denied.

READ_MEDIA_IMAGES / READ_MEDIA_VIDEO: selected or authorized media. READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (Android 12 and earlier) and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (Android 9 and earlier): legacy compatibility. MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE: browse, edit, move, and copy shared-storage files. Grant only when full file management is needed.

QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES: identify installed apps and read name, package, version, size, and signature digest; also detect companions such as Termux. Used for the app-list tool and compatibility checks, not advertising profiles.
POST_NOTIFICATIONS (Android 13+): show download, scheduled-task, or background-operation status. Tasks may still run if denied, but notifications will not appear.

REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES: open the Android APK installer after you download an update. Android requires separate “install unknown apps” permission and your confirmation. The app cannot install silently.

com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND: execute commands approved by you or the agent after Termux authorization. Shizuku and Root are separately enabled under System Permissions. Review every Shell/Root command because these capabilities are high risk.

Go to Settings → General → App permissions, or Android Settings → Apps → Lyra Code → Permissions/Special access.
Revocation stops new access through that permission but does not automatically erase previously saved local data. Delete it in the app, clear app data, or uninstall.

Use Root or Shizuku Shell for directories the app process cannot read directly, including Android/data, Android/obb, and /data. Normal permissions remain preferred; the selected channel is used only for restricted paths.
